la:verb:prolato.html:
prōlāto, āvi, ātum, 1, v. freq. a.
profero
.
To lengthen, extend, enlarge (not in Cic.; syn.: distendo, extendo; profero, differo): agros,: villam,: rem rusticam,, praef. § 19: effugium, : vitam,to prolong,.—
Of time, to put off, defer, delay, postpone (class.; cf.: profero, differo), id (malum) opprimi sustentando ac prolatando nullo pacto potest,: dubitando et dies prolatando,: diem ex die,: bellum,: bellum indies, Dietsch; cf. : consultationes,: seditiones, Dietsch: nihil prolatandum ratus,: prolatando aliquantum extraxerant temporis,.

la:adj:prolixus.html:
prō-lixus, a, um, adj.
laxus
,
stretched far out, long, broad (syn.: latus, spatiosus).
Lit. (not in Cic.): capillus passus prolixus, Umpfenb. (Fleck. prolixe): comae,: barba, (Forbig. promissa): caudae (opp. breves),: villi,: arbores,: ramus,: cervix,: statura,; cf.: prolixo corpore erat,: tunicae,. —Comp.: arator prolixior,taller, stouter,: prolixiora quaedam nascuntur,.—
Trop.
In gen., long, extended (ante- and postclass.): prolixae aetatis homines,i. e. of great age,; cf.: prolixioris temporis spatium,: non tam prolixo provolat ictu,far-reaching, distant,: si cognitio prolixiorem tractatum habeat,.—Sup.: labor (with largus), Mai.—Neutr. adverb.: prolixum ejulare,greatly, violently,. —
In partic.
in speech, prolix (post-class.): cujus exemplum, ne sim prolixus, omisi,—
Comprehensive in meaning (post-class.): existimo longe esse amplius, prolixius, fusius in significandā totius prope civitatis multitudine mortales quam homines dixisse,—
Of circumstances, favorable, fortunate (class.): rebus secundis atque prolixis atque prosperis, Cato ap. : cetera spero prolixa esse his duntaxat,.—
Of disposition and conduct, well-disposed, obliging, courteous (Ciceron.): prolixa beneficaque natura,: animus libens et prolixus,, C, 4: Ariobarzanes in Pompeium prolixior,.—Hence, adv.: prō-lixē, largely, abundantly, copiously (class.): capillus passus prolixe et circum caput Rejectus neglegenter, Fleck. (Umpfenb. passus prolixus): prolixe cumulateque facere aliquid,: prolixe et celeriter facere aliquid,, A, § 6: prolixe fuseque laudare,: promittere,: in quo (delectu) parum prolixe respondent Campani coloni,do not announce themselves in very great numbers,: arbores prolixe foliatae,.— Comp.: largius prolixiusque fruere,: fabulari,: accipit hominem prolixius,: fovere aliquem,; cf.: et factus in agoniā, prolixius orabat,more earnestly,.

la:noun:proles.gloss: offspring, children, progeny, descendants, a line of descendants, family, race
senses: offspring, children, progeny, descendants, a line of descendants, family, race
la:noun:proles.html:
prōles, is (
gen. plur. prolum, ), f.
pro and root al- of alo, to nourish, whence olesco in ad-olesco, etc.; cf.: suboles, indoles
.
Lit., that which grows forth; esp. of human beings, offspring, progeny, child, descendant; and collect., descendants, race, progeny, posterity (mostly poet.; but cf.: nec fugerim dicere prolem, aut subolem aut effari, etc.,; cf. , and v.in the foll. the passages from Cic.; syn. progenies). —Poet.: propagando procudere prolem,to bring forth, produce children,: prolem est enixa gemellam,: laudantur simili prole puerperae,; : di Romulae genti date remque prolemque,: et pulchrā faciat te prole parentem,: felix prole parens,: tua postuma proles,: ferrea proles, the iron race, Poët. ap. : aënea,: argentea,: proles Ausonia,the Ausonian race,: dic mihi, Teucrorum proles,.—In prose: praeclara Brutorum atque Aemiliorum proles, Dietsch; : proles illa futurorum hominum,race,.—Of individuals (poet.): Ulixi,i. e. Telemachus,: proles tertia Phorcus,: Clymeneïa,i. e. Phaëton,: Apollinea,i. e. Æsculapius,: deūm certissima proles,: egomet Neptunia proles,.—Of deities: Saturni altera proles,: Bacchi rustica proles,i. e. Priapus,: Cyllenia proles,: fulminis,i. e. Bacchus,; cf. : Jovis,.—Of animals: hinc nova proles per herbas Ludit,: duellica equorum,; ; : jam maris immensi prolem, genus omne natantum,; . —Poet., of plants: et prolem tarde crescentis olivae,i. e. the fruit,; cf.: naturae contenta manu Zephyrique favore

Parturit (tellus), et tantā natorum prole superbit, Alan. Anti-.—In plur.: privignasque rogat proles, Col. poët. 10, 163.—

Transf.
Youth, young men, : sternitur Arcadiae proles,.—
The testicles (post-class.): polimina sunt ea, quae nos proles verecundius dicimus,; .

la:verb:proluo.html:
prō-lŭo, lŭi, lūtum, 3, v. a.,
to wash forth or out, to cast out (mostly poet. and in postAug. prose; not found in Cic.; once in Cæs.; v.infra).
Lit.: genus omne natantum Litore in extremo ... fluctus Proluit,; ventrem,i. e. to cause diarrhœa,.—
Transf.
To wash off or away: tempestas ex omnibus montibus nives proluit,: impetus aquarum proluit terram,; cf.: silvas Eridanus,; .—Hence, *
Trop., to make away with property: pecuniam prandiorum gurgitibus,to squander, dissipate,.—
To moisten, wet, wash: in vivo prolue rore manus,: ensem,i. e. with blood,: cruor proluit pectora,.—Poet., of drinking: leni praecordia mulso Prolueris melius,: se pleno auro,; multā prolutus vappā,: nec fonte labra prolui caballino,.—In comic lang.: cloacam (i. e. ventrem), to wash out the stomach, i. e. to drink one's fill, .—
To overflow, inundate (postclass.): prolutas esse regiones imbribus, App. de Mundo, p. 73, 26.

la:noun:proluvies.html:
prōlŭvĭes, ēi, f.
proluo
,
an overflow, inundation (class.): Romae et maxime Appia ad Martis mira proluvies, (Bait.); : alvi,i. e. filth cast forth, excrements,; ; : foedissima ventris,.

senses: which served them for previous exercise
la:verb:proludo#2.html:
prō-lūdo, si, sum, 3, v. n.,
to play or practise beforehand, to prelude.
Lit.: et sparsā ad pugnam proludit harenā,.—Absol.: sic ubi prolusit, etc.,; .—
Trop.: sententiis, quibus proluserint, which served them for previous exercise, * : jurgia proludunt,: per has mortalis aevi moras illi meliori vitae longiorique proluditur,: cum per ista prolusum est, crescunt maria,: prima per legatos habita certamina, cum hinc Domitius et Thorius, inde Hirtulei proluderent,opened the contest,: prolusit dolor per ista noster,; ; .

la:adj:proletarius.gloss: belonging to the lowest class of citizens, who, lacking property, contributed to the State with their offspring instead
senses: belonging to the lowest class of citizens, who, lacking property, contributed to the State with their offspring instead
la:adj:proletarius.html:
prōlētārĭus, ĭi, m.
proles
.
According to a division of the people by Servius Tullius, a citizen of the lowest class, who served the State not with his property, but only with his children (proles), a proletary: qui aut non plus mille quingentum aeris aut omnino nihil in suum censum praeter caput attulissent, proletarios nominavit, ut ex iis quasi proles [id est quasi progenies] civitatis exspectari videretur,; cf ; Fragm. XII. Tab. ap. ; Enn. ib. (Ann. v. 189 Vahl.): proletarios lucrari plures,: proletarium capite censum, dictum quod ex his civitas constet, quasi proles progenie: iidem et proletanei, Müll.—*
Transf., adj., low, common: sermo,.

la:noun:prolixitas.html:
prōlixĭtas, ātis, f.
prolixus
.
Great length, breadth, or width, great extension (post-class.): terrae, App. de Mundo, p. 60, 21: colubra prolixitatis immensae,: temporis,length of time,. —
Of speech, prolixity: ne forte prolixitas fastidium audientiae pariat,: litterarum,.

senses: to collapse, decay, sink, decline, go to ruin
la:verb:prolabor.html:
prō-lābor, lapsus, 3, v. n.,
to glide forward, to slide or slip along, to fall down (class.; in Cic. most freq. in a trop. sense).
Lit.: at Canis ad caudam serpens prolabitur Argo, Cic. poët. N. D. 2, 44, 114; : ruit prolapsa moles, of the sea, Att. ap. : collapsus pons, usque alterius initium pontis prolabi eum leniter cogebat: alii elephanti pedibus insistentes, alii clunibus subsidentes prolabebantur,to slide along ... slide forward, sqq.: velut si prolapsus cecidisset, terram osculo contigit. : equus prolapsum per caput regem effudit,falling down,: ex equo,: ex arbore altā prolapsus,; ; cf.: prolapsus in cloacae foramen,: prolapsa Pergama,fallen down, fallen to ruin,: Laodicea tremore terrae prolapsa,.—
Trop.
To go forward, go on, to proceed or come to, fall into any thing: me longius prolapsum esse, quam ratio vestri judicii postularit, have gone farther, i. e. have said more, : libenter ad istam orationem tecum prolaberer,would go on, be led on,: in misericordiam prolapsus est animus,: in rabiem,: ad seditiones,: ad jurgia,: ad superbiam,fin.; .—
To slip out, escape: ne quod ab aliquā cupiditate prolapsum verbum videatur, (9, 18).—
To fall, fail, err: timore,: cupiditate,: cupiditate regni,: nimio juvandi mortales studio,.—
To fall to decay, to sink, decline, go to ruin: huc unius mulieris libido est prolapsa, ut, etc.,; cf.: eo prolapsi sunt mores, ut, etc.,: ita prolapsa est (juventus), ut coërcenda sit,: ad id prolapsae,: in aliquod dedecus,: prolapsum clade Romanum imperium,: rem temeritate ejus prolapsam restituit,; : studio magnificentiae,.—
To fall away from grace (eccl. Lat.), .

la:verb:prolongo.html:
prolongo, āvi, 1,
v. [pro-longus], to lengthen, prolong, extend (late Lat. for prorogo, profero, duco): dies,: iniquitatem suam,; Hilar. ad loc.; ; : sermonem,.

la:verb:proloquor.gloss: to speak out, utter, declare, say
senses: to speak out, utter, declare, say
la:verb:proloquor.html:
prō-lŏquor, cūtus (quūtus), 3,
v. dep. n. and a.
In gen., to speak out, utter, declare, say (mostly ante-class. and poet.; not found in Cic., Cæs., or Quint.): prolocutum (dicimus), cum animo quod habuit, extulit loquendo, Müll.: hoc profiteri et proloqui advorsum illam, Enn. ap. (Trag. v. 384 Vahl.): miserias Medeai caelo atque terrae, id. ap. (Trag. v. 291 Vahl.): cogitata,: verbum,; cf.: proloqui quicquam verborum,: aliquid apud aliquem,; so, apud aliquem,: vera,: falsum,: pervagatissimus ille versus, qui vetat Artem pudere proloqui quam factites,: nunc quam rem oratum huc veni, primum proloquar,; so with interrog.-clause: quid sentiatis proloquimini, Auct. B. Afr. 44 fin.; with acc. and inf., .—Absol.: ut occepisti, perge porro proloqui,.—*
In partic., to foretell, predict: proloquar, atque utinam patriae sim vanus haruspex, (4, 12), 59.

la:noun:prolatio.html:
prōlātĭo, ōnis, f.
profero
.
A bringing forward, putting forth, adducing, pronouncing, etc.: vocis,utterance,: verbi intellegibilis,; cf.: Latinorum nominum prolatione, v. l. for pronuntiatione,.—
A setting forth, mentioning: exemplorum,.—
A putting forward, advancing.
Lit.: finium,extension, enlargement,; ; ; Hilar. Trin. 4, 3.—
A putting off as to time, a deferring, delaying, delay, postponement: judicii,: rerum,: diei,.—Absol.: omnem prolationem suspectabant,; so in plur., ; .

la:noun:proloquium.html:
prōlŏquĭum, ĭi, n.
proloquor
. *
An introduction, preamble, Paul. ex Müll.; v. prologium.—
An assertion, proposition, axiom (class. Lat. pronunciatum), the Gr. ἀξίωμα, Varr. ap. ; cf. : disjunctivum,.—
A judicial sentence: sub uno proloquio cunctos jubet occidi,; .

la:noun:prolapsio.html:
prōlapsĭo, ōnis, f.
prolabor
.
A slipping, falling: ingredi sine casu aut prolapsione,.—
A falling or tumbling down: aedificiorum prolapsiones,.—
Trop., an error, misstep (late Lat.): intempestiva temeritas et prolapsio,; Ambros. de Noë, 14, 49; .
